SuperUnicode is the native character encoding of OpenWindows. It is 1:1 compatible with Unicode, carries its own machine-instruction control plane, and grows without limit through plugins.

Explore the standard Get SUCD 0.1.0

What is SuperUnicode?

SuperUnicode is the character encoding built into the OpenWindows kernel. Strings, filenames and data files are SuperUnicode streams by default — rendered directly by the kernel with no transcoding. It is organized into three spaces:

Unicode Compatibility Space

0x000000 – 0x10FFFF

Identical to Unicode, codepoint-for-codepoint. If Unicode releases a new version or adds new codepoints, this space still matches — forever.

System Control Plane

0x110000 – 0x11FFFF

Where machine instructions live: the BANcode Registry for diagnostics, warnings, communication and soft-fault codes.

Native SuperUnicode Space

0x120000 – 0x7FFFFFFF

The open field of OpenWindows’ own codepoints. Beyond it, the Extended system extends the space without any ceiling.

Why SuperUnicode?

Native

The kernel speaks one character system end-to-end. No code pages, no transcoding layers, no ambiguity.

Unicode-compatible

The low range is a permanent 1:1 bridge. Every Unicode codepoint exists in SuperUnicode with the same value.

Instruction-grade

Codepoints can be machine instructions. The SCP gives the kernel diagnostics, traps and control, not just text.

Unbounded

ExtSUCS has no ceiling. Plugins declare ranges above 0x7FFFFFFF and mount them securely at boot.

SuperUnicode Extended extends the default runtime ceiling of 0x7FFFFFFF with plugin-provided codepoints. Every plugin is verified by a checksum gate, mounted read-only as a SuperUnicode Plugin Partition (OWFS), and registered in the ExtSUCS registry. Learn about Extended »
